newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil seen posting trade deficits in 1997 - CNI.
newsitem.headline: Brazil seen posting trade deficits in 1997 - CNI.

text.p: Brazil is likely to continue showing trade deficits in 1997, despite an expected slight improvement in the country's exports, the National Industry Confederation (CNI) said in a report.

The CNI said exports are likely to grow somewhat in response to export-boosting measures introduced in 1996, which included new credit lines and tax exemptions, while imports will expand in tandem with the economic growth.
But exports are not expected to increase significantly in the short-term due to a number of factors, including foreign exchange policy and restrictions to Brazilian exports in key foreign markets.
Last year Brazil posted a record trade deficit of $5.576 billion, with exports of $47.747 billion and imports of $53.286 billion.

The CNI also said it expects Brazil to show a higher current account deficit in 1997, but noted it will be easily financed by growing foreign direct investment, particularly with progress in the country's privatizations.
In 1996, Brazil's current account deficit was 3.27 percent of the country's gross domestic product (GDP), up from 2.49 percent of the GDP in the previous year.
Brazil's foreign exchange and monetary policies are also likely to remain unchanged this year, with domestic interest rates falling at a moderate pace, the report added.
